turns.patient_response: I feel like I have to keep re-checking and re-doing things before and after every drive, or else something terrible will happen and it’ll be my fault. It's gotten to the point where I just can't seem to stop doing it.

turns.patient_response: Yes, I really do. Even though a part of me knows it's stupid and excessive to keep checking the car, the urge is just too strong to fight off. I get so terrified that if I don't do it, something horrible will happen and it will be completely my fault.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes an intrusive, persistent urge and a terrifying fear that something horrible will happen if they do not act, which characterizes an obsession.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient admits to repetitive checking behavior ('keep checking the car') that they recognize as 'stupid and excessive', which directly indicates a compulsion.

turns.patient_response: These checks take up a massive amount of time because I have to do them before and after every single ride, and I have to restart the whole thing if I get distracted. It’s completely taken over my life; I’ve been turning down lucrative driving shifts, falling behind on my CDL exam prep, and bailing on my friends.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes performing time-consuming 'checks' before and after every ride and having to restart them if distracted, which represents checking compulsions and repeating rituals.

turns.patient_response: Yes, I constantly get these awful pictures in my head of me missing a red light or a wheel falling off and causing a family to die, which loops endlessly and makes my chest feel tight. I feel forced to check my doors, trunk, and maps in a strict order just to try and stop those terrible things from happening.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes experiencing persistent, intrusive, and distressing mental images of causing fatal accidents that loop endlessly.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient reports feeling compelled to perform repetitive checking behaviors (doors, trunk, maps) in a strict order to prevent the feared events.
